title: Rage bait: How online anger makes money
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: social media content designed to provoke an emotional reaction so that people engage with the content thereby generating income for the online creator
as one thing (X) happens repeatedly, another thing (Y) happens more as a result
encourage someone to do or feel something unpleasant or violent; stir up; provoke; rouse
trying to influence or control someone to your advantage
the number of people viewing a particular website, television programme etc.
feelings, often hidden or unconscious, either for or against an idea or a group of people

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English, I'm Phil.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是BBC学英语的“6分钟英语”节目，我是菲尔。

sentences.en: And I'm Beth. If you use the internet, and nearly everyone does, you’ve probably read headlines like this: You won’t believe what plastic surgery this celebrity has had done!
sentences.zh: 我是贝丝。如果你上网的话——几乎所有人都在上网——你可能读过这样的标题：你绝对不会相信这位名人做了什么整容手术！

sentences.en: Known as clickbait, headlines like these are used to grab your attention and make you read more.
sentences.zh: 这类被称为“标题党”的标题，目的就是吸引你的眼球，让你阅读更多内容。

sentences.en: But now, a new trend called rage bait is spreading across social media.
sentences.zh: 但现在，一种名为“愤怒诱饵”的新趋势正在社交媒体上蔓延。

sentences.en: Rage bait is online content designed to make you angry or outraged.
sentences.zh: “愤怒诱饵”是指旨在让你感到生气或愤怒的网络内容。

sentences.en: In this programme, we’ll explore the trend of rage-baiting, and, as usual, we’ll learn some useful new vocabulary, all of which you can find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 在这个节目中，我们将探讨制造愤怒诱饵的趋势，像往常一样，我们会学到一些实用的新词汇，你都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到它们。

sentences.en: Great, but first it’s time for my question, Beth, which is about the two terms we’ve been using: 'clickbait' and ' rage bait '.
sentences.zh: 太好了，但首先是时候公布我的问题了，贝丝，这个问题关于我们一直在使用的两个词：“标题党”和“愤怒诱饵”。

sentences.en: Both contain the word, 'bait', but what is its actual meaning?
sentences.zh: 这两个词都包含“bait（诱饵）”这个词，但它的实际意思是什么？

sentences.en: Is bait: a) a strong feeling of anger? b) food put on a hook to catch fish or animals? c) a piece of computer software?
sentences.zh: 诱饵是：a) 一种强烈的愤怒感？b) 放在钩子上用来捕鱼或捕捉动物的食物？c) 一段计算机软件？

sentences.en: I am fairly confident that it is b) – food put on a hook.
sentences.zh: 我相当确信答案是 b）——放在钩子上的食物。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we'll find out the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。嗯，我们将在节目后面揭晓正确答案。

sentences.en: Here’s how rage bait works: a creator posts a provocative piece of content online, a message maybe, or a video.
sentences.zh: “愤怒诱饵”是这样运作的：创作者在网上发布一段挑衅性的内容，可能是一条消息，也可能是一个视频。

sentences.en: People see it, feel outraged, and comment angrily.
sentences.zh: 人们看到它，感到愤怒，并进行愤怒的评论。

sentences.en: Others see it, like it and share it around.
sentences.zh: 其他人看到它，点赞并四处分享。

sentences.en: Either way, the content creates interest, increases internet traffic and makes money for the creator.
sentences.zh: 无论哪种方式，这些内容都会产生关注度，增加网络流量，并为创作者赚钱。

sentences.en: Here’s marketing strategist, Andrea Jones, explaining more to Megan Lawton, presenter of BBC World Service programme, Business Daily: The more content they create, the more engagement they get, the more that they get paid.
sentences.zh: 以下是营销策略师安德里亚·琼斯向BBC世界服务部节目《商业日报》主持人梅根·洛顿做出的更多解释：他们创作的内容越多，获得的互动就越多，他们得到的报酬就越多。

sentences.en: And so they will do anything… some creators will do anything to get more views because the more views they get, the more that they get paid, even if, even if, those views are negative or inciting rage and anger in people.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会做任何事……一些创作者会为了获得更多浏览量而做任何事，因为他们获得的浏览量越多，得到的报酬就越多，即使，即使这些浏览量是负面的，或者是在煽动人们的狂怒和愤怒。

sentences.en: Andrea, how is rage bait different to clickbait or other online tactics? […] As a marketer, I'm always, you know, coaching my clients and talking to them about using hooks in their marketing, right?
sentences.zh: 安德里亚，“愤怒诱饵”与“标题党”或其他网络策略有什么不同？……作为一名营销人员，你知道的，我一直在指导我的客户，跟他们谈论在营销中使用“钩子”，对吧？

sentences.en: And I think the difference between a hook and rage bait or even its long-lost cousin, clickbait content… When we think about a hook, to me a hook accurately reflects what's in that piece of content and it comes from a place of trust, whereas rage-baiting content is designed to be manipulative.
sentences.zh: 我认为“钩子”与“愤怒诱饵”甚至它的失散多年的表亲“标题党”内容之间的区别在于……当我们想到一个“钩子”时，对我而言，“钩子”准确地反映了那段内容里有什么，它源于信任，而“愤怒诱饵”内容则旨在具有操纵性。

sentences.en: Andrea says the more reaction a post gets, the more money the creator makes, even if the reactions are hateful.
sentences.zh: 安德里亚表示，一条帖子获得的反应越多，创作者赚的钱就越多，即使这些反应是充满仇恨的。

sentences.en: She uses the structure, the more one thing happens, the more something else happens, to show that as one thing happens repeatedly, so another thing increases as a result.
sentences.zh: 她使用了“the more... the more...”的结构，来表明当一件事反复发生时，另一件事也会随之增加。

sentences.en: For example, the more you practise English, the more you’ll improve.
sentences.zh: 例如，你练习英语越多，你的进步就会越大。

sentences.en: It doesn’t matter that the content is designed to incite outrage – to encourage unpleasant or violent reactions.
sentences.zh: 内容旨在煽动愤怒——鼓励令人不快或暴力的反应——这并不重要。

sentences.en: That’s why Andrea thinks rage bait is worse than clickbait.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么安德里亚认为“愤怒诱饵”比“标题党”更糟。

sentences.en: While clickbait is more truthful about its content, rage bait is manipulative, meaning it tries to influence something to its own advantage.
sentences.zh: 虽然“标题党”对其内容的真实性更高，但“愤怒诱饵”具有操纵性，这意味着它试图为了自身利益去影响某些东西。

sentences.en: So, it’s not hard to see why many people think rage bait is toxic.
sentences.zh: 所以，不难理解为什么许多人认为“愤怒诱饵”是有毒的。

sentences.en: So, if you’re wondering why people react in the first place, listen as Dr William Brady explains the psychology behind rage bait to BBC World Service’s, Business Daily: If you are an influencer and you want to figure out, ‘Well, how do I get more eyeballs on my content?’ Well, you need to exploit those biases we have in our psychology because that's the content we’ll pay more attention to.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你想知道为什么人们一开始会有这种反应，请听威廉·布拉迪博士向BBC世界服务部的《商业日报》解释“愤怒诱饵”背后的心理学：如果你是一个网红，你想弄清楚，“嗯，我怎么才能让更多人看我的内容？”那么，你需要利用我们心理学中的那些偏见，因为那是我们会投入更多注意力的内容。

sentences.en: In turn that's the content that algorithms will amplify, which ultimately means more advertising revenue.
sentences.zh: 反过来，这也是算法会放大的内容，这最终意味着更多的广告收入。

sentences.en: Influencers want more eyeballs on their content – more people to view their website or social media posts – and use human psychology to do it.
sentences.zh: 网红们希望有更多人关注他们的内容——更多人浏览他们的网站或社交媒体帖子——并利用人类心理学来做到这一点。

sentences.en: Psychologically speaking, we all have biases – feelings – which are often unconscious, either for or against a certain idea or group of people.
sentences.zh: 从心理学上讲，我们都有偏见——各种感觉——它们通常是无意识的，要么支持，要么反对某个特定的想法或一群人。

sentences.en: Biases are emotional, and since listening to our emotions has been vital to the evolution of the human species, creators know that provoking our emotions will grab our attention.
sentences.zh: 偏见是情绪化的，既然倾听我们的情绪对于人类物种的进化至关重要，创作者就知道，激起我们的情绪将抓住我们的注意力。

sentences.en: So, what can be done to combat rage bait?
sentences.zh: 那么，可以采取什么措施来打击“愤怒诱饵”呢？

sentences.en: Well, we could all take a moment to think before reacting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们都可以在反应前花点时间思考一下。

sentences.en: And remember that by sharing something outrageous you might be making things worse, while also making the creator richer.
sentences.zh: 并且要记住，通过分享一些令人发指的事情，你可能正在让情况变得更糟，同时也让创作者变得更有钱。

sentences.en: OK, Phil, let’s reveal the answer to your question.
sentences.zh: 好的，菲尔，让我们揭晓你问题的答案。

sentences.en: You asked me what 'bait' is. I did. And the correct answer is b) food put on a hook to catch a fish or an animal, and isn’t that what you said, Beth?
sentences.zh: 你问我什么是“诱饵”。我是这么问的。正确答案是 b）放在钩子上用来捕鱼或捕捉动物的食物，贝丝，这不就是你说的吗？

sentences.en: It is, yes. Right again! OK, let’s recap the vocabulary we’ve learned in the programme, starting with rage bait, social media content designed to provoke anger, thereby encouraging people to engage with it.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。又答对了！好的，让我们回顾一下我们在节目中学到的词汇，从“愤怒诱饵”开始，这是一种旨在激起愤怒的社交媒体内容，从而鼓励人们与之互动。

sentences.en: The structure, t he more… the more… describes the situation when one thing happening repeatedly results in another thing happening too.
sentences.zh: 结构“the more... the more...”描述了当一件事反复发生导致另一件事也发生时的状况。

sentences.en: To incite someone means to encourage them to do or feel something unpleasant or violent.
sentences.zh: “煽动”某人意味着鼓励他们去做或感受到令人不快或暴力的事情。

sentences.en: The adjective, manipulative, describes trying to influence or control someone to your own advantage.
sentences.zh: 形容词“操纵性的”描述的是试图为了你自己的利益去影响或控制某人。

sentences.en: Eyeballs is an informal word for the number of people viewing a particular website or television programme.
sentences.zh: “眼球”是浏览某个特定网站或电视节目的观看人数的非正式说法。

sentences.en: And finally, biases are feelings, often unconscious, either for or against an idea or a group of people.
sentences.zh: 最后，“偏见”是各种感觉，通常是无意识的，要么支持，要么反对某种想法或一群人。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. Goodbye for now!
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟时间又到了。先到这里，再见！

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
